- **self**: Connection Pool Tuning (12/3)

## How it works

- [statement] Tune maxPoolSize against observed behavior. When the number of in-use connections reaches maxPoolSize, the next request waits, so raising it supports more concurrent requests (and the tuning guide advises raising it when database load is low and few connections are active). If database CPU is higher than expected and logs show more connection attempts than expected, decrease maxPoolSize or reduce application threads. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning/ · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-1-client-configuration/, https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/advisors/checks/mongo-high-connections.html, https://www.percona.com/blog/tuning-percona-clustersync-for-mongodb-performance/
- [statement] A nonzero minPoolSize keeps a floor of connections in each server pool; the driver reopens sockets if the total drops below the minimum. It can reduce connection-creation time at startup and helps workloads that need ready connections when traffic spikes. A MongoClient with maxIdleTimeMS and minPoolSize set to 0 is optimal for workloads with sustained low activity, because the pool can close unused connections (in the Node.js driver this works for minPoolSize 0 from version 6.18.0). Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning/ · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/, https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-1-client-configuration/
- [statement] maxConnecting is separate from maxPoolSize: it is the maximum number of connections a pool may be establishing concurrently (default 2), while maxPoolSize is the maximum number of connections opened in the pool. Raising maxConnecting lets the client establish connections to the server faster but increases the chance of connection storms; too low a value can cause heavy throttling and increased tail latency for clients checking out connections. maxConnecting is supported by all drivers except the Rust driver per the manual overview, although the Rust driver guide lists max_connecting. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/ · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/, https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/connection-monitoring-and-pooling/connection-monitoring-and-pooling.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md
- [statement] For MongoDB drivers that implement a connection pool, maxPoolSize caps all connections in that pool, including checked-out and available connections. When the cap is reached, new operations wait for a connection; waitQueueTimeoutMS can bound that wait. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/connection-monitoring-and-pooling/connection-monitoring-and-pooling.md · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md
- [statement] MongoDB's tuning guide recommends increasing maxPoolSize (or the number of active application threads) when database load is low and there are few active connections, and decreasing maxPoolSize or application threads when database CPU usage or connection attempts are higher than expected. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-1-client-configuration/
- [statement] Track actual connection use and acquisition behavior when tuning. IBM documents db.serverStatus().connections counters such as current, available, rejected, and totalCreated, while MongoDB documents waitQueueTimeoutMS as a bound on waiting for pool checkout. (medium confidence) Sources: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mongodb-gen2?locale=en&topic=databases-for-mongodb-gen2-managing-connections ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md — https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mongodb-gen2?locale=en&topic=databases-for-mongodb-gen2-managing-connections · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use minPoolSize when a measured startup or warm-connection need justifies keeping connections ready. Because the minimum applies to each pool, include every MongoClient and topology server when estimating the idle connection floor; on-demand pools avoid keeping that baseline when cold connection setup does not affect the workload. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/connection-monitoring-and-pooling/connection-monitoring-and-pooling.md, https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-1-client-configuration/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A MongoClient maintains pools for the servers in its deployment topology, so the configured pool limit is not a deployment-wide connection total. MongoDB's tuning example multiplies maxPoolSize by replica-set members for one application's outgoing sockets and by application servers for incoming sockets at each mongod; each additional MongoClient contributes its own pools. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-1-client-configuration/
- [statement] waitQueueTimeoutMS is the maximum time a thread can wait for a connection to become available; 0 means no limit. MongoDB's tuning guide advises increasing maxPoolSize when database load is low and there are few active connections, and decreasing it when database CPU is higher than expected. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/connection-pool-overview.md · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-1-client-configuration/, https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mongodb-gen2?locale=en&topic=databases-for-mongodb-gen2-managing-connections

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In the Node.js driver, waitQueueTimeoutMS bounds how long a request can wait for a socket when the pool is full; when it expires, the request fails with a connection error. This setting bounds queue latency rather than increasing pool capacity, so choose it against the request's latency budget. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/ · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://github.com/mongodb/specifications/blob/master/source/connection-monitoring-and-pooling/connection-monitoring-and-pooling.md, https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/building-resilient-applications-with-amazon-documentdb-with-mongodb-compatibility-part-1-client-configuration/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Each MongoClient maintains a connection pool for each server in its topology, and maxPoolSize caps each of those pools. In the Node.js driver, each MongoClient also opens up to two monitoring connections per server on top of the pooled connections, so estimate total connections across client instances and topology members before setting the cap. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/connection-pool-performance-tuning/ · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/, https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/databases-for-mongodb-gen2?locale=en&topic=databases-for-mongodb-gen2-managing-connections
- [statement] Current MongoDB driver guides list different maxPoolSize defaults: 100 for Node.js and 10 for Rust. Defaults are driver-specific, so check the target driver's exact release before relying on a default or copying a setting. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools.md — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/ · keywords: Connection Pool Tuning · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/rust/current/connect/connection-options/connection-pools/
